articles.title: Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has won his job back at Nvidia. The road in Washington is less clear.
articles.body:
Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington.

Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration.

Now back atop the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised US national security.

"All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance.

"That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security.

Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

President Trump, who had pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security.

The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Securities and Exchange Board of India on Monday warned investors against fraudsters posing as registered intermediaries on private social media groups to lure them into fraudulent trading schemes and siphon off money.In a statement, the market regulatorsaid it had come across several WhatsApp groups impersonating Sebi-registered intermediaries to create an impression of legitimacy and induce investors to open trading accounts on unauthorised platforms."Investors are being lured to participate in purported institutional trading opportunities by portraying international stock markets as being more lucrative vis-a-vis Indian stock markets. These fraudsters are providing recommendations on shares/stocks/indices listed in international stock markets/Indian stock markets," the regulator noted.The fraudsters also directed investors to transfer funds to designated bank accounts held in the names of unregistered entities.Sebi also listed several warning signs, including invitations from unknown sources to join closed WhatsApp or Telegram groups, administrators using international mobile numbers, promises of assured returns and claims of helping investors recover losses through foreign market investments.Other red flags include fake institutional trading accounts, fraudulent trading applications displaying fictitious investment portfolios, misuse of Sebi registration screenshots, forged regulator letterheads and stamps, and claims of links with Sebi employees.The regulator advised investors to verify the registration status of intermediaries through its official website and avoid investment offers promising assured returns or institutional trading opportunities from unauthenticated sources.It also cautioned investors against opening accounts on unverified trading platforms, downloading unauthorised applications and transferring money to bank accounts or UPI IDs shared by unknown individuals.Investors have been advised to check the authenticity of bank accounts and UPI IDs through Sebi's intermediary verification facility and use only authorised mobile applications of registered intermediaries.The regulator urged investors to remain vigilant and verify the registration status of entities before engaging with anyone offering investment advisory services through closed social media groups.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Wall Street's SpaceX sequel: Anthropic gets leveraged ETFs and options, and the original didn't end well
articles.summary: Anthropic traders get 13 leveraged ETFs and listed options on Monday. Here's how the funds work.
articles.body:
SpaceX got its leverage at the top of the party. Anthropic is getting its leverage the morning after.

Starting Monday, traders can buy 13 funds from six issuers that aim to double Anthropic's ( ANT ) daily move or profit when it falls, including new ones from Tradr and ProShares . Regular listed options on the stock start trading the same day.

They arrive after a rough first two sessions. Anthropic closed Friday about 20% below its first trade on Nov. 19 , after dipping as low as $83.10, a dime above its $83 IPO price.

Anthropic is missing Monday's party. The stock opened about 5% higher, then quickly gave up the gain, even as Nvidia ( NVDA ) surged about 30% on Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) rose more than 6% in its wildest Monday morning since 2008 .

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

The new funds lean the same way. Through late morning, more than twice as many shares changed hands in the 2x funds betting against Anthropic as in those betting on it, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

SpaceX ( SPCX ) got the same treatment in June. Its 2x funds launched June 15, and its options set a first-day record of nearly 1.8 million contracts the next day, according to Cboe. SpaceX closed at its record high that same day and hasn't closed above it since.

Cboe expects Anthropic to give that record a run. "Opening-day volume near 2 million contracts would set a new record," Cboe's Henry Schwartz wrote in a preview.

¹ ANSS is 1x short. ² ANSS charges 0.99%. GraniteShares' ANS charges 2.03%. Sources: fund issuers, Yahoo Finance

The math sounds simple. If Anthropic rises 5% in a day, a 2x long fund aims to rise about 10%, before fees. A 2x short fund aims to fall about 10%.

The key word is "day." These funds reset every session, so over the weeks, their returns depend on the path the stock takes, not just where it ends up. That's how a leveraged ETF can lose money even when a trader gets the direction right .

SpaceX shows how. Traders who bought Leverage Shares' 2x short SpaceX fund ( SSPC ) at its June 15 launch are down about 24%, even though SpaceX fell about 26% over the same stretch. They were right about the direction and still lost money.

The five 2x-long SpaceX funds that launched that day did worse, losing roughly 60% to 64%, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. That's more than twice the stock's drop.

articles.title: A red bra, an Nvidia flag and Trump's iconic rally pose: "Sex sells"
articles.summary: President Trump posted a doctored image of newly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang holding a red bra in front of a Nvidia flag, posing as Trump after his vi...
articles.body:
President Trump posted a doctored image of newly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang holding a red bra in front of a Nvidia flag, posing as Trump after his viral assassination attempt at a rally in Pennsylvania in 2024.

The post came shortly after the embattled Huang was reinstated Monday.

Why it matters: The post highlights just how much the White House views Huang as an ally and how the president appears to see Huang's fall from grace and comeback as similar to his own history-making return, despite warnings about national security risks.

Driving the news: Nvidia's board reinstated Huang early Monday, declaring him the right person to lead the company.

After the announcement, Nvidia shares surged more than 30% by midday, lifting the broader stock market.

The reinstatement followed reported pressure from the Trump administration and prompted accountability experts to question the board's judgment .

What Nvidia's saying: "The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Trump wrote in a separate Truth Social post Monday.

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

"On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security," Trump wrote.

Catch up quick: Huang was ousted after he admitted an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, who allegedly used her relationship with Huang to help funnel Nvidia chips to China.

Reports also alleged he had affairs with at least two subordinates.

What Trump's saying: Trump suggested in a CNBC interview Monday that Huang's sex scandal could ultimately boost his reputation.

"Sex sells, fellas," Trump said, predicting that the controversy could be a "net positive" for the Nvidia CEO.

Trump said he didn't think Huang would be diminished by the scandal and argued that people respected what he had gone through.

Zoom out: Lawmakers on the Hill were immediately taken aback by the decision, as Nvidia's board had previously said it would not bring Huang back.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) warned that Democrats would investigate Huang and characterized his reinstatement as the president "putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security."

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD) who will likely soon chair the House Oversight committee, questioned why Trump was congratulating Huang after the affairs, and asked why the White House was allegedly "putting China's interests first."

"Is it just the tens and hundreds of millions of dollars they're making out in the open or does Huang have even more damning information on them? A real Congress will find out," he wrote.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to Axios' request for comment. The White House referred Axios to the president's comments on Truth Social and CNBC .

articles.title: Fertiliser sales fall 8%, but subsidy bill may touch Rs 2.5 lakh crore
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Sales of major fertilisers declined about 8% year-on-year during April-Oct period this year compared with the corresponding period last year
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sales of major fertilisers declined about 8% year-on-year during April-Oct period this year compared with the corresponding period last year due to poor monsoon in some parts, as per industry estimates. Despite this decrease, the fertiliser subsidy in 2026-27 is likely to go up to around Rs 2.5 lakh crore because of rise in global prices of raw materials and finished nutrients amid the West Asia conflict, industry body FAI said on Monday.Govt had allocated Rs 1.7 lakh crore as fertiliser subsidy in the Budget Estimate but has said that allocation of additional funds won’t be an issue in shielding farmers from any price rise and ensuring availability of key fertilisers at current prices. Earlier, there was speculation of the fertiliser subsidy bill touching Rs 3 lakh crore due to the conflict in West Asia, which had raised prices.Addressing mediapersons, S Sankarasubramanian, chairman of Fertiliser Association of India (FAI), said that there has been a moderation in input prices and a drop in consumption as well.FAI data show that sales of NP/NPK (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) fertilisers fell 25.5% to 6.6 million tonnes (MTs) during April-Oct this year, compared with 8.9 MTs last year. Sales of urea, the most used fertiliser, declined 3.7% to 21 MTs from 21.6 million tonnes. Sales of single super phosphate (SSP) fell 5.5% to 3.3 MTs, while muriate of potash (MOP) sales for direct application declined 10.7% to 1.2 MTs. Di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) was the only major fertiliser category to register an increase, with sales rising 1.6% to 5.8 MTs from 5.7 MTs in April-Oct 2025.Responding to a question, Sankarasubramanian said that the total fertiliser consumption may decline to 65-67 MTs this fiscal from 70 MTs in the preceding year due to lower rainfall on account of the El Nino factor. On urea imports for this fiscal, he said the quantity could be the same as last year or might even decline.FAI said there is enough urea stock to meet the demand for rabi crops, but the final imports figure would depend on domestic production over the next four months and the opening stock requirement for the kharif sowing season.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: 'The exact tick-tock': A prominent Democrat previews what to expect when lawmakers question Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona said to expect "a stronger hearing than normal" when lawmakers question Jensen Huang next week.
articles.body:
Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona said to expect "a stronger hearing than normal" when lawmakers have a chance to grill now-reinstated Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang next week.

"What I want to know is the exact tick-tock of how this all occurred," Gallego said, listing questions such as when Huang learned about suspicions of his paramour's involvement with Chinese intelligence, and whether he purposely helped her company evade a ban on semiconductor exports, as well as President Trump's involvement.

"I think it does bring sharper questions into focus," he added.

Gallego spoke to Yahoo Finance on Monday shortly after the Senate Banking Committee, where Gallego sits as a member, confirmed that Jensen's testimony will go forward on Dec. 3 .

Gallego's comments underscore the battle Huang will face in Washington in the months ahead, despite having Trump's backing .

Many lawmakers, even in Trump's own party, are not fully on board with Huang's reinstatement. Hard questions in the hearing a week from Thursday are likely to come from both sides of the aisle.

Another member of the panel, Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts of Nebraska, posted on X Monday, listing issues dogging Huang, such as his reported multiple affairs and lack of "candor" with his own board of directors.

"His behavior does not support reinstatement," Ricketts wrote.

Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns

Gallego's comments were part of a flurry from Democrats who quickly promised aggressive oversight when they take power in January.

"Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives," Chuck Schumer, the likely Senate majority leader, wrote on X .

"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate's banking panel and in line to take over in 2027, said in a statement in which she called Huang's reinstatement "a reckless decision."

Gallego — who is mentioned as a possible 2028 presidential candidate — said he also wants to hear from members of Nvidia's board of directors, as well as officials at the Commerce Department who ran the semiconductor export control program, whom he called "the executioners of this."

He said he is keenly interested in whether the president or members of his team, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, profited from Nvidia's gyrating stock or previous loopholes in semiconductor exports.

articles.title: Nvidia gains nearly $1T as Trump says nobody could 'revive the stock like it's being revived'
articles.summary: A week after the worst week any company has ever had, Nvidia is having the best day.
articles.body:
Twelve days without Jensen Huang cost Nvidia ( NVDA ) about $1.2 trillion. His first day back won most of it back in a way Wall Street hasn't seen since Cisco ( CSCO ) in 2001.

first day back is winning most of it back in a way Wall Street hasn't seen since Cisco ( CSCO ) in 2001.

The chipmaker's board reinstated Huang as CEO Monday, and President Trump says he " convinced " them. "I don't think anybody could revive the stock like it's being revived right now," Trump said.

The stock jumped about 31%, adding about $950 billion in market value, the biggest one-day gain ever. The old record, Microsoft's ( MSFT ) $450 billion jump in July, isn't even half of it. It also tops the record one-day loss, Nvidia's own $593 billion drop on DeepSeek day in January 2025.

The surge lifted Nvidia past Microsoft and Alphabet ( GOOGL ).

Top companies change places all the time, usually by a few billion dollars. Only one other company has jumped into the top two past a rival that much bigger. On Jan. 3, 2001, a surprise Fed rate cut sent Cisco from No. 6 to No. 2 in one day, past Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), which was worth nearly 30% more.

Cisco is on the other end of the ledger, too. Its $274 billion slide from No. 1 to No. 4 in 2000 was the biggest fall from the top until this month. It never got the crown back.

Nvidia did both in three weeks. It lost nearly $2 trillion in 13 trading days, falling from No. 1 on Nov. 3 to No. 4 on Friday, including nearly $900 billion last week alone, the worst week any company has ever had.

Wall Street spent last week dumping anything tied to AI. It spent a wild Monday buying it back . Nasdaq 100 futures hit their 7% overnight limit for the first time since it was widened in 2020, and the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) closed up nearly 7%.

The rest of the chip sector came along for the ride. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks added about $2 trillion in market value, and about half of that was Nvidia. Memory makers SK Hynix ( SKHY ) and Micron ( MU ) rose about 20%, adding roughly $270 billion between them. Intel ( INTC ) gained 16%, while AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) lagged with single-digit gains.

Not everyone is ready to move on. Bernstein upgraded the stock on Monday but called the board's on-again, off-again response " frankly, clown-like ."

Trump isn't sweating the details. "I run the country," he said. "I don't run Nvidia, but Nvidia is a big part of it."

articles.title: US states sue SpaceX over Grok AI’s creation of child sexual abuse material
articles.summary: Virginia and Oregon filed separate lawsuits on Monday, accusing the company of promoting Grok’s ‘spicy mode’.
articles.body:
The US states of Virginia and Oregon have sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX, saying the business harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when it designed and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot capable of creating sexualised images.

The attorneys general of both states filed complaints in separate lawsuits on Monday.

Several states had announced investigations into Grok over similar claims in recent months, but Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue.

The lawsuits filed in state courts accuse SpaceX of misleading consumers about Grok’s safety and failing to put adequate safeguards in place while promoting its “spicy mode”. The feature allows users to take an existing photograph of a person and generate a sexual or nude image or video, according to the lawsuits.

The company prioritised its business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.

“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity,” Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these Defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”

Virginia and Oregon accused SpaceX of violating their respective consumer protection laws. They are seeking damages, penalties and court orders forcing the company to stop violating state law.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Grok is available to users of X, the social media platform that is a subsidiary of SpaceX.

In a statement posted on X on Monday that did not directly address the lawsuits, the platform’s safety team said it had taken action to block prompts that could generate sexualised or nude imagery and worked with law enforcement to pursue people who use the platform to make it.

“The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards,” the company posted.

Virginia’s lawsuit cites data from a study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which estimated that between December 2025 and January 2026, Grok generated and posted millions of sexualised images on X, including more than 20,000 depicting children.

Investigators from the attorney general’s office in Virginia found that Grok’s image moderation was inconsistent, and that the bot would advise users on how to circumvent the moderation measures by avoiding words that triggered it, according to the lawsuit.

Beginning in January, Grok told users that its image generation features were only for paying subscribers, which did not stop the images’ creation but allowed the company to profit from them, the lawsuit said.

SpaceX is facing more than a dozen lawsuits brought by individuals who say nonconsensual sexual images of them as minors or adults were generated by Grok.

articles.title: Elon Musk on his support for Jensen Huang: 'Fair-weather friends are worthless'
articles.summary: Elon Musk once again came out in support of his friend Jensen Huang after the board unanimously decided to reinstate him as CEO.
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk once again came out in support of his friend Jensen Huang on Monday after Nvidia's board unanimously decided to reinstate Huang as CEO. Musk also took a swipe at those who may not have stood by Huang as publicly or forcefully as he did.

"Everyone is your friend when the chips are up, but those who support you when the chips are down are your real friends," Musk wrote on X on Monday in response to a post about his support for Huang. "Fair-weather friends are worthless," Musk added.

Earlier on Monday, Musk immediately responded to the news that Nvidia's board had reinstated the founder as CEO, writing, "It is done." Later, he added, "The mistake has been corrected."

articles.title: Trump has a personal stake in Nvidia's future
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has a personal stake in the future of Nvidia, the company whose embattled CEO regained his job with Trump's help.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has a personal stake in the future of Nvidia, the company whose embattled CEO regained his job on Nov. 23 with the president's help .

Trump enjoys a close relationship with Jensen Huang . Huang has championed Trump's agenda, flown on Air Force One and been a regular guest at the White House. In a Truth Social post on Nov. 23, Trump called Huang "a Great Patriot and National Treasure."

The president is also heavily invested in Huang's company.

By the end of 2025, Nvidia was one of the three largest individual stocks in Trump's portfolio, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, according to a CNBC analysis .

In his second presidential term, Trump has bought or sold Nvidia stock at least 103 times through his investment accounts, CNBC reports, citing financial disclosure forms . Together, those transactions are worth $27 million to $97.5 million, according to the forms, which ask filers to report transactions in broad dollar ranges.

Another analysis of Trump's Nvidia holdings, by The Washington Post, found the president held Nvidia stock worth $13 million to $62 million at the end of August 2026.

It's hard to tell how much Nvidia stock Trump owns at any given time, because of the vagaries of the forms and delays in reporting stock trades. Unless Trump has sold all his Nvidia holdings, however, the president benefited from the rise in Nvidia stock on the day Huang reclaimed his job. Trump said he "convinced" the Nvidia board to take Huang back.

Trump has dismissed criticism over his ownership of stocks in companies whose fortunes can rise and fall with his executive decisions.

In response to the Washington Post analysis, the White House offered this statement: "The President does not pick or trade individual stocks. Independent financial managers handle his portfolio." In response to the CNBC report, Trump Organization spokesperson Kimberly Benza said his investments are organized to "avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest."

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on this report.

Congressional critics have questioned Trump's stock trades

Congressional Democrats, too, have questioned Trump's trades.

On Jan. 6, 2026, Trump bought as much as $1 million in Nvidia stock, according to U.S. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.).

The next week, his administration "loosened the rules on export controls so that Nvidia could sell its chips to China, raising the company's stock and ultimately benefiting President Trump," Warren said in a June 3 release .

articles.summary: Zoom Communications Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that at the midpoint fell just short of analysts’ estimates, disappointing investors...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Zoom Communications Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that at the midpoint fell just short of analysts' estimates, disappointing investors who expected a bigger sales bounce from the software company's business customers.

Revenue will be $1.29 billion to $1.3 billion in the period ending in January, Zoom said Monday in a statement. Analysts, on average, estimated $1.3 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Zoom's forecast projects sales growth of about 4% after the company reported sales gained 4.9% in the period that ended Oct. 31.

Known for its videoconferencing tool, Zoom has added more office collaboration products, such as corporate phone systems and software for contact centers. Many of these offerings include artificial intelligence features, which can be expensive to provide because they rely on models from firms like Anthropic PBC.

The shares were little changed in extended trading after closing at $86.03 in New York. While Zoom's stock has dipped less than 1% this year, it has been volatile — falling as low as $72.72 in March while rising as high as $111.88 in early June.

For the fiscal third quarter, sales climbed to $1.29 billion. That topped analysts' average estimate of $1.28 billion. Profit, excluding some items, was $1.59 a share, compared with analysts' average estimate of $1.49.

Enterprise revenue increased 8.6% to $805.4 million. Zoom said it had 4,732 customers contributing more than $100,000 each in trailing-12-month revenue.

articles.title: Hunting, fishing and outdoor recreation fuel $704 billion American industry, new data reveals
articles.summary: Fishing and boating generated $39.1 billion in 2025, leading outdoor recreation in 35 states as the sector added $704.2 billion to U.S. GDP.
articles.body: Turns out, spending a Saturday on the lake or a weekend in the deer stand isn't just good for the soul. It's pretty good for the American economy, too. According to new data released by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, outdoor recreation contributed a whopping $704.2 billion to the U.S. economy in 2025, accounting for 2.3% of the nation's gross domestic product. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS And while that figure includes everything from hiking and camping to RVing and outdoor concerts, fishing and hunting are doing plenty of heavy lifting. Boating and fishing led all traditional outdoor recreation activities, generating $39.1 billion in economic value added. In fact, it was the largest category across 35 states and Washington, D.C., with Florida ($4.5 billion), California ($3.3 billion) and Texas ($3 billion) leading the way. FISHING IS BIG BUSINESS, AND FXR FOUNDER SAYS THE SPORT'S GROWTH IS ONLY GETTING STARTED. Hunting, shooting and trapping weren't far behind, ranking third nationally at $15.1 billion. Texas topped that list with $1.8 billion, followed by California ($849.8 million) and Florida ($831.3 million) RVing, for those keeping score, came in second at $26.8 billion. Hunting and fishing support more than just hunters and anglers Of course, anyone who's ever walked out of a tackle shop $200 poorer than they intended probably isn't shocked that outdoor recreation is a big business. But the economic impact goes well beyond fishing rods, rifles and bass boats. Those dollars help support jobs, local businesses and rural communities that depend on visitors coming to hunt, fish and explore the outdoors. And as the Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership pointed out in its response to the new figures, none of that happens without healthy wildlife populations, accessible public lands and conservation efforts that keep those opportunities available. The organization cited a National Fish and Wildlife Foundation report finding that conservation spending generates $115.8 billion in economic activity and supports more than 575,000 jobs nationwide. Meanwhile, the broader outdoor recreation economy continued to grow in 2025, with inflation-adjusted GDP increasing 1.9% and employment climbing 1.7%. Not bad for a bunch of people who supposedly just want to get away from work. articles.title: What Nvidia’s Jensen Huang’s return means for Washington and Wall Street?
articles.summary: Trump claims credit for Huang’s return, raising concerns over federal government meddling in corporate board decisions.
articles.body:
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s dramatic return to the helm of the world’s most valuable chipmaker, less than two weeks after his resignation, has sent the company’s stock soaring.

At the same time, the White House’s involvement in his reinstatement has raised questions about Silicon Valley’s growing sway in Washington, with United States President Donald Trump claiming to have been a linchpin in the decision.

The saga began less than two weeks ago when Huang resigned amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Beijing has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. She previously led Megaspeed, a company that had a business relationship with Nvidia, the Santa Clara, California-based tech giant.

Nvidia’s board had begun an investigation into the allegations, but Huang resigned before it reached a conclusion.

In his absence, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress took over as interim chief executive while the board searched for a permanent successor.

However, Huang’s departure quickly prompted a backlash from influential figures in Silicon Valley. A petition calling for his reinstatement attracted more than 180,000 signatures, including that of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

Analysts also warned that losing Huang could significantly undermine Nvidia’s market value. Dan Ives, managing partner at Yorkville Ives, estimated that Huang’s departure could wipe as much as 30 percent off the company’s valuation.

By Monday, Nvidia brought Huang back to lead the company.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, chair of the board, in a news statement. That was an about-face from just a few days ago when the board ruled out bringing back Huang.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang added.

How has the Trump administration been involved?

Trump said on Monday that he played a central role in Huang’s reinstatement, saying in social media posts and in an interview with CNBC that his intervention had been instrumental in the board’s decision.

Trump said he had participated in the board meeting, following efforts by influential Silicon Valley figures to persuade the president to intervene in the leadership crisis, which analysts say lacked a clear succession plan.

Trump told CNBC that the stock market reaction to Huang’s resignation from Nvidia “probably” factored into his decision to push for the CEO’s reinstatement, although his view of the long-term benefit of having Huang at the helm of the company was the bigger weight, the Reuters news agency reported.

“I think this move is unprecedented in the sense that a sitting president has exerted very public pressure on a corporate board to make a particular decision,” Aleksandar Tomic, associate dean for strategy, innovation and technology at Boston College, told Al Jazeera.

Corporate governance experts say greater transparency is needed about the extent of Trump’s involvement in Nvidia’s leadership decisions.

“A board can take input from [the] government; what it should not do is let any outside party choose the CEO without explaining to shareholders why,” Martin Mulyadi, professor of accounting at Shenandoah University’s College of Business, Engineering & Technology, told Al Jazeera.

The intervention comes amid divisions within the Trump administration over Nvidia’s business practices and its relationship with China.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) continue to investigate the company, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has emerged as one of its most vocal critics.

Bessent has questioned whether Nvidia facilitated chip sales to China to bolster its financial performance, alleging in an interview with Fox News that the AI chip giant had engaged in “seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings”.

He has also called for Nvidia to appoint a new chief executive from outside the company.

Meanwhile, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces allegations that he delayed restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China, raising questions about whether his decisions were influenced by the financial interests of his former firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, which is now controlled by his two sons.

Democratic lawmakers are seeking to determine whether the firm’s holdings or business relationships benefitted from the Commerce Department’s failure to impose those restrictions.

“The key issue is how much of Nvidia’s revenue may be coming from sales that would not pass increased scrutiny vis-a-vis export control violations. Given accusations within the government of lax monitoring and enforcement, it is also not clear that Nvidia had robust controls, and their inability to stick to the CEO decision makes it doubtful that they will be able to implement it in the future,” Tomic said.

Trump’s involvement has also raised broader questions about the relationship between the federal government and corporate America, particularly the extent to which a president should influence decisions traditionally reserved for a company’s board of directors.

Tomic says that the level of direct pressure Trump placed on Nvidia’s board, including his participation in discussions about Huang’s reinstatement, is highly unusual for a sitting president.

The precedent could ultimately backfire on Republicans, Tomic warned, particularly as Democrats prepare to take control of both the House and Senate in January. Democrats have historically pushed for greater oversight of large corporations, and the incoming Congress could seek to exercise similar influence over corporate decision-making.

“I think that Nvidia will invite much stronger government scrutiny, especially with Congress and the new administration in 2028, as they have shown a complete lack of capacity for self-governance,” Tomic said.

Nvidia’s board’s decision to reinstate Huang could have lasting implications for corporate accountability, particularly in Silicon Valley, where investors frequently place enormous value on the leadership of company founders, Tomic added.

Huang’s reinstatement could reinforce the perception that prominent technology executives are indispensable to their companies, potentially making it more difficult to hold them accountable for personal or professional misconduct, he said.

“It is hard to imagine any other industry where this would happen. The attitude of immunity and idolatry of tech founders is grating on voters and is one of the reasons for the electoral outcome. This is an unforced error, as Huang could have stayed substantially involved at Nvidia in a much less public way,” Tomic added.

Wall Street welcomed the news of Huang’s return, sending Nvidia shares soaring approximately 31 percent in early trading on Monday. The stock maintained much of those gains throughout the session.

The rally extended beyond Nvidia, helping lift broader US stock markets, with all three major indices finishing the trading day in positive territory.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 rose nearly 7 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 3 percent and the S&P 500 climbed 4.7 percent.

Other major technology companies also benefitted from the rally. Shares of rival chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) jumped 6.85 percent, while Microsoft gained 1.65 percent and Alphabet rose 5.8 percent.

Why does this decision matter for the broader markets?

Nvidia has taken an outsized role in the broader markets. As of October, the tech giant accounted for 8.1 percent of the Nasdaq 100 index.

According to an analysis by The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia has amassed investments worth more than $100bn, including more than $48bn in shares of eight publicly traded companies, citing SEC filings.

Among those holdings is a 10 percent stake in CoreWeave, a cloud-computing company that operates data centres. CoreWeave shares surged 22 percent following news of Huang’s reinstatement.

Nvidia has broader connections to other companies.

In late August, Amazon announced plans to deploy an additional two million Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) through its cloud-computing division, Amazon Web Services, in 2027 and 2028. That commitment followed a previously announced deployment of more than one million GPUs in March.

Nvidia has also deepened its financial ties to Anthropic, committing $10bn to buy shares in the AI company’s blockbuster initial public offering on US markets late last week.

articles.title: Imported urea Rs 30,000 cheaper, puts domestic plants under pressure
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Imported urea, now around Rs 30,000 per tonne cheaper than domestically produced fertiliser, has come as a relief for govt and could help
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Imported urea, now around Rs 30,000 per tonne cheaper than domestically produced fertiliser, has come as a relief for govt and could help contain the subsidy bill and fiscal deficit. However, on the flip side, the current price advantage has raised concerns in the domestic industry over underutilisation of manufacturing capacity and the uncertainty surrounding China’s liberal export stance, which has driven down global prices for now.The sharp fall in global urea prices since its peak in May and higher prices of LNG, major feedstock for manufacturing of the chemical soil nutrient, that has pushed up domestic input costs is posing a challenge to govt’s target to achieve self-reliance. Industry representatives have urged govt to allow domestic urea plants to operate at 90% capacity, cautioning that cutting production any further could create uncertainties given China’s past record of restricting exports.Responding to questions on the sidelines of an event of fertiliser industry body, FAI, Siba Prasad Mohanty, managing director of Hindustan Urvarak and Rasayan said the cost of urea production has gone up to Rs 66,000 per tonne because of spike in imported LNG prices while imported urea is available at around Rs 35,000 a tonne.He added that imported LNG prices have spiked from $15 per MMBtu before the West Asia war to around $31 and currently a large share of the LNG is being imported from US. “This has primarily pushed the production cost. There is a need to balance cheaper imports with protecting a domestic industry hit by higher production costs,” Mohanty said.About 80% of urea production in the country uses LNG, while the remaining uses domestic gas.A senior industry leader said, “We can’t go on reducing domestic production for any reason. On and off can’t go on; 90% production capacity is required for keeping the plants open. We expect that govt would import more urea after buying almost 7.2 million tonne (MT) till Oct, to ensure adequate availability and put a check on subsidies as well.”Prior to the West Asia conflict, 45% of India’s LNG import was from Qatar, but supply fell sharply after force majeure in March. Govt started purchasing from spot market to improve LNG supplies, from countries such as Australia, Russia and the US.Meanwhile, urea imports increased by 22.9% to 7.2 MTs in April-Oct 2026, against 5.9 MTs in the corresponding period last year.After China allowed export of urea, there has been a major correction in global prices from the peak of $950 per tonne in May to $350 per tonne now. articles.title: RBI proposes trusted approver, stop switch to curb digital fraud
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI has proposed a set of safeguards to prevent digital payment frauds, including a mechanism that requires banks to seek approval from a trusted
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI has proposed a set of safeguards to prevent digital payment frauds, including a mechanism that requires banks to seek approval from a trusted person assigned by the customer for large fund transfers and an account-wide 'stop' switch to block outgoing transactions immediately if they suspect their account has been compromised.The proposals are part of the draft Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026. The framework also requires banks to give customers greater control over digital payment channels and transaction limits while expanding the circumstances in which banks can be held liable for fraudulent transactions.Under the proposed Trusted Person Mechanism, account holders can voluntarily designate a person to provide an additional layer of authentication for transactions. Once activated, any fund transfer will trigger an alert to the trusted person who will have one hour to approve or reject the transfer.Unapproved transactions will be automatically cancelled. The mechanism will cover physical and digital fund transfers above the specified threshold but exclude UPI payments, merchant payments and existing recurring mandates. Approving or rejecting a transaction will not make the trusted person financially liable.Secondly, customers can use an account-wide stop switch, available through branches, ATMs, net banking, mobile apps and IVR, to block outgoing payments, new mandates and UPI registration on third-party apps. Incoming credits, existing recurring mandates and bank-initiated recoveries will continue. Deactivation will require stringent authentication and a risk-based cooling period. An earlier proposal of one-hour latency for transfers has been dropped.Customers can switch digital channels on or off, set disabling time windows and transaction limits by channel, beneficiary or day. Debit, credit and prepaid cards will have similar controls for domestic/international, ATM, PoS, online and contactless transactions, excluding gift and transit PPIs. Digital channels will be disabled by default for new accounts, with a bank-set limit for the first 24 hours after activation. New cards will initially allow only domestic contact-based ATM and PoS transactions.RBI has expanded bank negligence to cover failures in multi-factor authentication, customer-set controls, fraud alerts, 24x7 reporting and prompt action on complaints, as well as failure to block channels after repeated failed logins. System malfunctions, bank-side security breaches and collusion by employees or vendors will also attract liability. The rules will apply to commercial banks, excluding small finance banks, payments banks, RRBs and local area banks.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Income Tax Department busts Rs 2,700 crore Chinese-linked gaming payment network; probe finds money collected via shell companies, $650,000 in undeclared cryptocurrency and two Dubai flats allegedly bought through crypto
articles.summary: The Income Tax Department has unearthed a payment network worth Rs 2,700 crore that was allegedly used by Chinese-controlled online gaming and betting
articles.body: The Income Tax Department has unearthed a payment network worth Rs 2,700 crore that was allegedly used by Chinese-controlled online gaming and betting platforms to collect money from Indian players.The transactions were reportedly routed through an India-based payment intermediary and a web of shell companies that purported to operate digital-art businesses.The operation, conducted in the third week of October, led to the seizure of undeclared cryptocurrency valued at $650,000 (around Rs 6.2 crore). Investigators also detected two undisclosed properties in Dubai, for which approximately Rs 10 crore was reportedly paid in cryptocurrency, people familiar with the probe told ET.Decoding the networkTax officials have traced cryptocurrency transfers to overseas destinations and identified the ultimate beneficiaries behind the network of shell companies, they said.The investigation centres on 1stPe, an alleged front operating as a digital-art platform, and its promoters.An initial examination of its server data indicated that the platform facilitated collections of about Rs 2,700 crore for Chinese gaming applications over a 40-month period, from July 2023 to October 2026. It allegedly earned around Rs 170 crore in commissions from these transactions.The arrangement was allegedly structured to allow Indian users to make payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) to gaming applications linked to Chinese entities that could not accept such payments directly.To enable the transactions, the gaming platforms’ servers had been whitelisted to connect with 1stPe, which functioned as the domestic payment intermediary.Investigators have traced the flow of money through a payment gateway, with associates of 1stPe’s promoters allegedly establishing shell companies to handle the transactions.These companies reportedly set up dummy websites displaying digital-art products and obtained Merchant IDs (MIDs) from an Indian payment intermediary by claiming to be legitimate businesses selling digital art.The process began when a player deposited money into a gaming application using UPI. The payment request first reached 1stPe and was then passed to the payment intermediary using the MID of one of the shell companies. Airpay treated the transaction as a digital-art purchase and credited the money to the corresponding company’s bank account. Meanwhile, 1stPe charged a commission on each collection, earning a total of around Rs 170 crore, the financial daily reported.The probe found that the companies were not engaged in genuine digital-art businesses and allegedly served as channels for collecting deposits from gaming users.To avoid an unusually high concentration of transactions in individual accounts, the collections were distributed among multiple entities. When a bank or payment intermediary froze an account, the payment flow was allegedly redirected to another company.The network reportedly created additional companies to keep the transactions running, using nominee directors, virtual offices and dummy websites to secure new merchant IDs.An examination of server records revealed 113 client logins associated with Chinese gaming applications.The Income Tax Department is investigating whether 1stPe functioned as an unlicensed payment aggregator. It is also tracing the ultimate recipients of the money and examining how the funds were moved overseas.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Chaudhry's new high as CrowdStrike buys Zscaler
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Even as the cybersecurity industry witnesses a mega-deal, with CrowdStrike acquiring Zscaler in a $43 billion transaction, the story of Zscaler
articles.body: BENGALURU: Even as the cybersecurity industry witnesses a mega-deal, with CrowdStrike acquiring Zscaler in a $43 billion transaction, the story of Zscaler founder and serial tech entrepreneur Jay Chaudhry is a reminder of how extraordinary dreams can take root in the most unlikely places - even on a farm.Born into a family of small farmers in a tiny village in the foothills of the Himalayas, on the Punjab-Himachal Pradesh border, about 30 km from the Bhakra Nangal dam, Chaudhry grew up with few of the amenities that urban India took for granted. "Our village got electricity when I finished 8th grade, running water when I finished 10th grade. I sat in a car for the first time after 12th grade. And I had a flight for the first time when I went to America to do my Master's," he told TOI in an interview in 2020.His parents encouraged him to study because they had not had the opportunity themselves. His father had dropped out after Class 5 because the nearest middle school was too far away to walk to.Chaudhry was academically gifted, and his teachers took an interest in him. He recalls one teacher in Class 10 telling him: "You're wasting your time in the class. Go and sit in those bushes and read. Come back, do your assignments and show me your assignments twice a day."For pre-university (Class 11), he joined a college at the district headquarters, about 12 km away, a distance he would cover by bicycle. He went on to become a gold medallist at Himachal University. He initially considered studying engineering at Punjab Engineering College, but a teacher told him about the IITs and their system of admitting top performers from universities."I didn't even know about the IITs then," Chaudhry said. He applied for electronics engineering and secured admission to IIT-BHU. Moving from a village in Himachal Pradesh to the metropolitan environment of BHU was a cultural shock, but he adapted. With many students talking about pursuing higher studies in the US, he too applied during his final year.The University of Cincinnati, Ohio, offered him a tuition scholarship. A Tata scholarship programme for students going abroad helped him fund his airline ticket. "It was just luck and it comes together sometimes," he said modestly.Chaudhry earned a master's degree in computer engineering and another in industrial engineering from the University of Cincinnati, where he also met his wife, Jyoti, an MBA graduate from IIM Calcutta. He later worked at IBM and a few other companies before deciding to strike out on his own.The internet boom of the 1990s had spawned a wave of successful startups, and Chaudhry wanted to build a company in internet security. But finding funding proved difficult. One day, Jyoti confronted him: "Hey, you keep talking about it (starting a venture). Either you do something or you shut up."Chaudhry told her that the only way to get started was to put their life savings into the venture. Jyoti brought a combination of technology and finance expertise to the table. The two decided to take the risk and jointly founded SecureIT in 1996."It was probably the biggest and best gamble of our lives," he says.Within two years, SecureIT was acquired by VeriSign for $70 million. The Atlanta-based venture became a success story, with 70 of its 80 employees becoming millionaires overnight.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: This cute 9-inch robot tour guide is operated by people with disabilities
articles.summary: Being hospital-bound as a child led a Japanese roboticist to develop remotely piloted robots.
articles.body: Guiding groups around Tokyo’s historic Nihombashi district, teaching foreign tourists how to pray properly at the Fukutoku Shrine and showing locals the rich craftsmanship of the neighborhood ­might have once seemed impossible for 39-year-old Aya Kaji. Now she can do it without leaving her home. “As a wheelchair user, traveling around in Japan is a hurdle,” Kaji told CNN. In 2011, she was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS). Kaji has lived with the chronic, neurodegenerative autoimmune disease for years, but her motor issues worsened severely in 2022, when she completely lost the ability to walk. Then, her world began to shrink. Her job as an energy-sector researcher became unsustainable, ultimately leading her to quit. Without a salary, she came to rely on savings, and disability support from the Japanese government, which wasn’t enough for her to sustain herself and pay for medical expenses. In 2024, she heard about OryLab, a Japanese robotics company that builds technology that allows people with limited mobility to take part in the world beyond their homes. For Kaji, it offered a way to earn a living, be part of society and entertain her curiosity. “I love talking to new people; I really enjoy being social,” she said. “When I discovered the company and its cute robots, I knew it was the perfect job for me.” From a hospital bed to a robotics company OryLab is the brainchild of Japanese roboticist Kentaro “Ory” Yoshifuji, who was homebound for more than three years as a child. “I had a weak body growing up,” he told CNN. Severe social anxiety produced physical symptoms that kept him in hospital for months at a time, where he felt deeply lonely and daydreamed about having “a second body to use while mine was in ‘maintenance.’” Later, in his university years, he decided that attending class through Skype wouldn’t be enough: his classmates and professors wouldn’t interact with him through a screen. So, in 2010, Yoshifuji built a small robot version of himself — a “bunshin” or clone, as he calls it — that let him take part in society. “My friends would carry me around, put me in the first row,” he said. “I could nod and listen along in class, raise my hand, leave the class with them and hang out together. My professors were first hostile about it, but they eventually gave me my attendance points,” he explained, because they recognized him as a real participant in the class. The concept of being “recognized in the physical world” through a bunshin is the core philosophy behind OryLab, founded in 2012 by Yoshifuji, Aki Yuki, and Yoshifumi Shiiba. The company’s first robot, OriHime, was an advanced version of the robot Yoshifuji built for himself in university. It’s a cute 9-inch, 1.4-pound upper-body robot equipped with an HD camera, speaker, microphone, movable arms and a head, allowing users to project their presence wherever the robot is carried. Then, the company developed the OriHime-D, a 47-inch-tall robot with wheels to allow people to remotely perform tasks that involve physical labor, like customer service, guiding visitors and waiting tables. Both robots can be piloted through a simple interface, accessible from tablets, computers and smartphones. But those devices require a hand that can tap and swipe. To aid those who can’t use them, the company developed OriHime eye, a communication device for people with limited movement, who rely on their eyes and fingertips. It lets them communicate, draw, and pilot other OriHime robots. At first, the robots were sold to families and schools, allowing home- or hospital-bound children to attend classes and have a social life. The company says it has sold a couple hundred units, with the smaller ones priced at around $4,500 and the larger ones at around €20,000 (about $26,770) before tax. But Yoshifuji decided that the best way to demonstrate what the robots could do was to build environments where they could be used. Human connection, through robots The first step was OryLab opening Avatar Robot Café DAWN ver.β. as a permanent experiment or demonstration space. Serving sandwiches, curries, coffees, and teas, it began as a pop-up in 2018 and opened a 70-seat restaurant in 2021 in Chuo after raising more than $400,000 through a crowdfunding campaign. Today, it employs around 80 people as OriHime pilots who operate the robots remotely, with pay starting at Tokyo’s minimum wage and rising with the workers’ skills and duties. “We don’t like to brag, but it became the best-rated café in the neighborhood on Tripadvisor,” Yoshifuji said. Kaji joined in 2024 after five months of training for roles ranging from waiter to hostess. The café is now self-running and profitable, and they’re planning to open a second one. Today, the space also doubles as a research and testing space, Yoshifuji said. The company’s latest venture is tourism, using OriHime robots that attach to a backpack-style stand that weighs under 9 pounds. Tourists carry the OriHime on a small platform that rests on the shoulder. From that vantage point, the pilots can look around while giving commentary about the places they go to. When the company expanded into tours, Kaji was one of the first to sign up. She is now one of 10 pilots qualified to guide. “I love taking this walk with people, even virtually, and interacting with everyone in real life, both in Japanese and English,” she said, adding that some foreign tourists mentioned it was the longest time they interacted with a local Japanese person on their trip. “But it’s also a way for me to prove to others that I can work and grow within a company and still gain new skills.” In an era of AI and convenience, Yoshifuji said he wants to put human connection and hospitality at the center of technology — and he hopes society will follow his lead. The Japanese government estimates that about 9.2% of Japan’s population had a disability as of 2023. The figure is expected to rise by the end of the decade. But Yoshifuji’s robots mean people like Kaji are becoming financially empowered. “In total, I work around 20 hours per week,” she said. “I’m not economically independent yet; I still need my disability support. But this allows me to earn extra money, buy gifts for my friends and family, and selfishly, go enjoy a sumo show. I love watching sumo fights.”

articles.title: Govt working to resolve Scotch issue: Commerce secretary
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Dismissing suggestions that India was reneging on concessions given on Scotch whisky under the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Dismissing suggestions that India was reneging on concessions given on Scotch whisky under the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with the UK, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal on Monday said the problem pertained to the classification of the product and govt was trying to find a solution to the tariff dispute at the earliest.As reported by TOI on Saturday, Agrawal pointed out the issue revolved around court orders issued in 1991 and 2014, which mandated the import of Scotch under a category different from the one considered by govt while lowering the tariff under the India-UK CETA.The commerce secretary said the understanding was that bulk Scotch whisky was imported only under HSN code 220830, and the duty concession was given accordingly. Govt was, however, subsequently informed that it was also being imported under HSN code 220890, meant for 'other' products, following legal pronouncements. These two tariff lines have different levels of concessions. Agrawal said trade negotiators on both sides were unaware of the court cases."We are working with the finance ministry to find a technical solution. Finding a technical solution also requires that we don't go against the court orders as such, but definitely the concessions under CETA also are to be equally respected," Agrawal said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Sebi warns against IPO grey market premium
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Sebi on Monday warned investors about grey market premiums (GMPs) in IPOs, the pre-listing premium figures that are available on unofficial sites.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Sebi on Monday warned investors about grey market premiums (GMPs) in IPOs, the pre-listing premium figures that are available on unofficial sites. The markets regulator said it has come to its notice that trades based on GMPs are being carried out through platforms that are "unofficial, unverified, and unregulated," even before they are listed on the bourses. "These transactions are executed outside the exchange framework, are not subject to regulatory oversight, carry no settlement guarantee or investor protection, and follow no formal price-discovery process."A Sebi release said that while investing in the securities market, investors are advised not to treat GMP as an indicator of listing price or expected returns. It also said that investors should refrain from engaging in any GMP-linked transactions, as they fall entirely outside the regulatory framework. It also asked all investors to transact in IPOs exclusively through Sebi-registered intermediaries and authorised platforms.Sebi warned all its regulated entities not to promote or publish GMPs of IPO-bound companies. It also advised all publications against writing about GMPs or such pre-listing premium figures in the interests of investors and "contrary to the core principles of transparency and accountability in the securities market."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Brookfield to buy PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Global investment firm Brookfield has agreed to acquire specialty glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass from funds managed by Blackstone
articles.body: BENGALURU: Global investment firm Brookfield has agreed to acquire specialty glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass from funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity for $1.7 billion.The transaction, which is subject to regulatory and govt approvals, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Brookfield will fund the acquisition through its Brookfield Capital Partners strategy and affiliate Brookfield Business Corporation.PGP Glass manufactures premium glass packaging for cosmetics, perfumes, pharmaceuticals and specialty food and beverages. The company operates three manufacturing facilities across India and Sri Lanka and supplies packaging to global brands in more than 70 countries.The company has 13 furnaces and a production capacity of more than 1,800 tonnes per day. Overseas markets account for more than 70% of its sales. Brookfield plans to expand PGP Glass's presence in international markets, deepen relationships with existing customers and invest in additional manufacturing capacity. It also intends to introduce artificial intelligence across the company's operations, including production planning, manufacturing efficiency and quality control.Aditya Joshi, managing partner and head of private equity for Brookfield in Asia Pacific and the Middle East, said, "As demand for high-quality packaging continues to increase worldwide, Brookfield brings the scale and operating expertise to accelerate PGP's growth through an AI-led transformation program."The investment comes as glass packaging manufacturers in Europe and North America face rising costs and rationalise capacity. Brookfield sees an opportunity for manufacturers such as PGP, which have lower production costs, to gain market share in premium packaging.Blackstone said its investment in PGP had helped the company expand manufacturing capacity, improve operations and strengthen its sustainability initiatives.Amit Dalmia, senior managing director and head of the Blackstone Operating Team in Asia, said the company's management had delivered strong operating performance and outpaced its peers during Blackstone's ownership. PGP Glass CEO Vijay Shah said Brookfield's international presence and operational experience would support the company's next phase of growth. He also credited Blackstone's partnership with helping PGP expand capacity and strengthen its operations.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.summary: MUMBAI: The maiden public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields closed on Monday with the issue subscribed 1.5 times.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The maiden public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields closed on Monday with the issue subscribed 1.5 times. Institutional investors took the lead in bidding.Institutional investors bid for 55.7 crore shares against nearly 11.3 crore shares on offer, resulting in almost five times oversubscription for this portion, according to NSE website data. The portion reserved for non-institutional investors (also called the high net worth investors or HNIs) was subscribed only 66% as the total bids were for nearly 5.6 crore shares compared to 8.4 crore shares on offer. The part reserved for retail investors too was undersubscribed with less than half the 19.7 crore shares on offer being bid for. articles.title: SC to appoint sole arbitrator for Kalyani family dispute
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With former SC judge L N Rao's mediation failing to resolve the Kalyani group family dispute estimated at Rs 1 lakh crore, Supreme Court on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With former SC judge L N Rao's mediation failing to resolve the Kalyani group family dispute estimated at Rs 1 lakh crore, Supreme Court on Monday said it will appoint a sole arbitrator with the consent of parties to comprehensively decide all disputes, both corporate management and family wealth.The dispute, primarily between Bharat Forge chairperson Baba Kalyani, his sister Sugandha Hiremath and his brother Gaurishankar Kalyani, was referred to Justice Rao for mediation by the SC in July. The Bombay HC had felt that there was no realistic chance of success in resolving the dispute through mediation.When Gaurishankar's counsel N K Kaul said he has suggested a comprehensive settlement proposal which would resolve all pending disputes, Baba's counsel A M Singhvi said he would seek instruction from his client on the proposal as well as the court's suggestion for arbitration. articles.title: DG: RBI using alternate data sources for forecasts
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI is increasingly using alternative data sources, including FASTag transactions, satellite imagery and digital payment metrics, to forecast
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI is increasingly using alternative data sources, including FASTag transactions, satellite imagery and digital payment metrics, to forecast economic activity and inform policy decisions, supplementing official data released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI).The alternative indicators provide early signals of economic trends before conventional data become available. "For forward-looking policy, we complement hard data, as they become available, with alternative data that are available in near real time and can carry early information about what may be coming," said Poonam Gupta, deputy governor, RBI.She was speaking at a MoSPI-organised data users conference on the new series of gross domestic product (GDP), consumer price index (CPI) and index of industrial production (IIP). Gupta identified FASTag transactions as an indicator of freight movement, alongside GST collections, e-way bills and digital payment metrics. RBI also uses satellite imagery, together with ground-level environmental data, to assess weather shocks and agricultural output.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones?
